Definition: or συγχύνω from G4862 and χέω (to pour) or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind):--confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar.
BiblicalUsage: At Pentecost the multitude comes together and is confounded because every man hears the apostles speak in his own language, and at Damascus Saul confounds the Jews by proving that Jesus is the Christ. Confusion can be the crowd's bewilderment at God's work or the enemy's defeat by God's truth, and the difference is which side of the proof you stand on.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's truth confounds its opposers, and I hold that being confounded by God is the first step to believing Him.
